4. In 1980, the National Archives pulled the patent for X (1906) for a commemorative exhibit at the Smithsonian. When the exhibit ended, the document was supposed to go back to its high-security vault in Washington, D.C. Instead of being returned to its specific "Treasury Vault," it was accidentally misfiled into a massive, 15-foot-high stack of mundane patent records from the early 20th century.
Before it was found in the cave, the FBI actually investigated the possibility that the patent had been stolen by a rogue collector. Because the patent features the original signatures of the brothers, it was estimated to be worth millions on the black market. The FBI spent years tracking high-end auctions, only to realize the "thief" was actually a filing clerk’s honest mistake. Id X.
